questions.q: How is Zoca onboarding delivered to a prospect?
options: As a public self-serve sign-up they complete alone
As an assisted, desktop-first setup run with the prospect on a screen-share
As a downloadable mobile app installed before the demo
As an emailed login the owner figures out on their own
questions.explain: Onboarding is an assisted, desktop-first session run with the prospect on a screen-share, not a public self-serve sign-up.

questions.q: In what fixed order are the three AI agents introduced during agent setup?
options: Front Desk, Bookings, Discovery
Bookings, Discovery, Front Desk
Discovery, Bookings, Front Desk
Discovery, Front Desk, Bookings
questions.explain: The agents are introduced one at a time in the fixed order Discovery, then Bookings, then Front Desk.

questions.q: Where do a salon's services come from during onboarding?
options: They are imported automatically from the salon's current booking link and confirmed on a review screen
The owner retypes every service and price from scratch
They are copied from the salon's Google Business Profile
An AE enters them manually after the call ends
questions.explain: Services are imported automatically from the current booking link, then confirmed on a review-services screen before the website builds.

questions.q: What are the three sections of onboarding?
options: Discovery, Bookings, and Front Desk
Platform setup, agent setup, and formalities
Audit, demo, and migration
Sign-in, payment, and go-live
questions.explain: Onboarding is organized into three sections: platform setup, per-agent setup, and formalities.

questions.q: How long is the free trial, and when does the first charge land?
options: 14 days, charged on the first day
30 days, charged immediately
7 days, charged only after the trial ends
7 days, charged at the moment the card is added
questions.explain: The trial is 7 days and the first charge auto-bills only after the trial ends, like Netflix.

questions.q: Which payment methods are supported to start the trial?
options: Card only; PayPal and Apple Pay are not supported
Card, PayPal, and Apple Pay
PayPal or Apple Pay only
Bank transfer or card
questions.explain: A valid, funded card is required to start the trial; PayPal and Apple Pay are not supported.

questions.q: What happens to the contract when a business adds more agents later?
options: A brand-new contract must be signed and a new card added
The existing contract is augmented automatically with no re-signing and the same card
The trial restarts from day one
The business must book an offboarding call first
questions.explain: Adding agents later augments the same one-per-business contract automatically with no re-signing and the same card on file.

questions.q: How does a customer cancel during the trial?
options: By emailing a cancellation request
By letting the card expire on its own
By clicking a single cancel button in settings
By booking an offboarding call rather than flipping a switch
questions.explain: Cancellation isn't one click; it requires booking an offboarding call so there's a human conversation first.

questions.q: How many platform journeys are there, and what decides which one a prospect lands in?
options: Three journeys, decided by their plan tier
Five journeys, decided by the platform they run today
Five journeys, decided by how much they pay
Three journeys, decided by their location
questions.explain: There are five platform journeys, and the prospect's current booking platform determines which one they land in.

questions.q: What does the secure automated assistant do on the salon's platform?
options: It edits and updates the salon's existing system
It deletes the old platform after migrating
It reads their information read-only without changing their existing system
It charges the salon a connection fee
questions.explain: The secure automated assistant signs in to read the salon's current data read-only and never changes their existing system.

questions.q: How does pricing differ between the platform journeys?
options: There is no price difference; the journey only changes the setup steps
The flagship migration costs the most
Direct connection is cheapest
The secure automated assistant adds a surcharge
questions.explain: There is no price difference between journeys; the journey changes only the setup, not the bill.

questions.q: What does the flagship migration journey do?
options: Keeps the salon entirely on their old platform
Reads data read-only without moving anything
Connects two systems but changes nothing
Moves the salon fully onto Zoca's own bookings and payments
questions.explain: The flagship migration moves the salon fully onto Zoca's own bookings and payments as the end-state.

questions.q: How should you pitch Zoca onboarding in one line?
options: "Sign up online and explore on your own."
"Three steps, one screen-share, and you're live."
"Download the app and we'll call you later."
"Pay first, then we set everything up."
questions.explain: The flow doc pitches onboarding as "Three steps, one screen-share, and you're live."

questions.q: Roughly how long does getting a salon live with website, bookings, and AI receptionist take?
options: A full working day
About three business days
Well under an hour
Around two to three hours
questions.explain: The whole setup comes together in well under an hour.

questions.q: During Front Desk setup, what does the prospect do?
options: Connect platform, set up number, choose voice, set call forwarding, and run a test call
Only confirm services and prices
Import their booking link and build a website
E-sign the contract and add a card
questions.explain: Front Desk has the prospect connect the platform, set up a number, choose a voice, set call forwarding, and run a live test call.

questions.q: Why is the card-on-file step framed "like Netflix"?
options: Because Zoca streams training videos
Because the trial includes free movies
Because billing is handled by Netflix
Because you put a card down, get a free week, and aren't charged until it's up
questions.explain: The Netflix framing means a card on file starts a free week with no charge until the trial ends, and you can cancel.

questions.q: If a payment fails after the trial, what happens?
options: Access is cut off instantly
There's a short grace period to fix it before functionality closes
The trial automatically restarts
A second card is charged automatically
questions.explain: A failed payment triggers a short grace period to resolve it before access closes.

questions.q: What kind of business is onboarding built for today?
options: Multi-location chains only
Franchises with shared billing
Solo and single-location businesses (multiple staff are fine)
Online-only businesses with no storefront
questions.explain: Onboarding is built for solo and single-location businesses; multiple staff are fine but multiple locations aren't yet.

questions.q: Why must onboarding be confirmed on the current environment before a live setup?
options: Because the newest version lives in the demo/sandbox environment and production can lag
Because production is always more up to date
Because the prospect chooses the environment
Because pricing differs by environment
questions.explain: The newest version lives in the demo/sandbox environment and production can lag, so confirm the current environment first.

questions.q: Where are the salon's card details stored?
options: Directly by Zoca on its own servers
By the salon's current booking platform
By Zoca's billing provider, not by Zoca directly
Only on the owner's local device
questions.explain: Card details are stored by Zoca's billing provider, not held by Zoca directly.
